chunks: Another text: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, who said: He narrated to me Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal, who said: He narrated to us Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Dawud al-Raqqi, who said: I said to Abu Ibrahim Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him): May I be your ransom, my age has grown old, so narrate to me who is the Imam after you?
So he pointed to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), and said: 'He is your master/leader after me.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا: Abu al-Hasan al-Rida, the eighth Imam
key_terms.أَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Abu Ibrahim, a title for Musa ibn Ja'far (al-Kazim)
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: The Imam, the divinely appointed leader

ai.seo_question: Who did Imam al-Kazim appoint as his successor?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *‘Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* records the explicit appointment (naṣṣ) of Imam Musa al-Kazim, pointing to his son Abu al-Hasan Musa al-Rida as his successor. The use of the phrase 'this is your master' (ṣāḥibukum) underscores the authority and spiritual leadership inherent in the Imams, a key concept in Shia theology regarding the continuity of divine guidance. This event is historically significant as it solidifies the line of Imams during the late Abbasid period, reinforcing the doctrine of Imamate through direct designation.
